chunks: And in it is that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over the believers except over those who follow him from the polytheists.
And He did not grant them authority except to make known whoever believes in the Hereafter from whoever is in doubt about it.
And indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of all things.
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of Satan's authority over believers according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this narration within the Shia doctrine of *Khud'* (self-determination), clarifying that Satan's 'authority' is not coercive but persuasive, acting as a trial for those who voluntarily follow him. This distinction underscores the Shia view that believers are not bound by Satan's influence unless they choose to align with his whispers, thereby preserving human free will against divine predestination. The reference to Allah's omniscience serves as a reminder that this conditional authority operates within the broader framework of divine knowledge and ultimate justice.
